name: ServiceNow, Inc.
price_source: StockAnalysis.com (close Jun 22, 2026), corroborated by Yahoo Finance (~$95 Jun 21) and CNBC
owner_fcf_base: FY2026 owner FCF base ~$3,300M (reported FCF ~$5,650M at 35% margin on ~$16.1B rev, MINUS 100% SBC ~$2,350M). Reference: FY2025 owner FCF = $4,636M FCF − $1,955M SBC = $2,681M (~$2.60/sh). SBC is high at 14.7% of revenue / ~42% of FCF — the 100% SBC deduction is material and conservative. Per-share owner FCF FY2026 ~$3.20.

conservador.note: Phase1 g=15%, Phase2 declining to 8%, terminal 3%, WACC 10%. Pesimista-razonable: AI rotation compresses growth but franchise intact, FCF margin holds; +$8.6B net cash. Rev still grows mid-teens, not apocalyptic.

base.note: Phase1 g=20%, Phase2 declining to 10%, terminal 3%, WACC 10%. Tracks raised FY2026 guidance (sub rev +22%, cRPO +22.5%, FCF margin 35%); growth decelerates gracefully as base scales.

optimista.note: Phase1 g=24%, Phase2 declining to 12%, terminal 3%, WACC 10%. AI/Now Assist + platform expansion sustain low-20s growth longer; margin expansion to ~37% FCF.

multiple_metric: Forward non-GAAP EPS (FY2026 ~$4.24/sh, derived from price/fwd P/E)
multiple_rationale: 5y-avg fwd P/E ~52x (NOW historically 50-60x in 2021-2024). Applied a deliberate HAIRCUT to 32x fair multiple — a ~38% cut. The de-rating is partly STRUCTURAL not just cyclical: (1) higher-for-longer rates lift the discount rate vs the ZIRP era that supported 50x+, (2) a genuine AI-disruption risk premium on application software, (3) law of large numbers as NOW scales past $16B revenue. But 32x is still a premium multiple justified by ~22% growth, 35% FCF margin, net cash, and cRPO durability — well above the panic-level 22x now. iv_multiple = $4.24 × 32 = $135.78.
structural_change: No fundamental deterioration. The -56% drop from the split-adjusted 52w/ATH (~$211) is a fear_rotation / de-rating, not a broken business: FY2026 guidance was RAISED in Q1 (sub rev +22-22.5%, non-GAAP op margin ~31.5%, FCF margin ~35%), Q1 rev +22% YoY, cRPO +22.5%. The only genuinely structural shifts are valuation-side, not business-side: (1) a higher rate regime compressing software multiples, (2) AI-disruption risk premium on app software, (3) decelerating growth as the base scales. These are captured via the multiple haircut (52x→32x) and a 10% WACC, not by impairing the cash flows.
sanity_notes: Price $93.01 and ~1.03B shares (post 5-for-1 split Dec 18, 2025) reconcile: 93.01 × 1.03B = $95.8B vs reported $95.92B mcap — mcap_sanity_ok=true. All IV/share outputs ($108.65-$183.63 DCF; $135.78 multiple; $136.22 reconciled) sit at 117%-197% of the $93.01 price, inside the 30%-300% magnitude band, so no shares/currency/units error. DCF and multiple anchors converge tightly (within ~1%: $136.88 vs $135.78), raising confidence. Weights 0.40 DCF / 0.60 multiple — proven, stable, net-cash compounder warrants leaning on the multiple anchor (pure DCF under-credits decades of high-ROIC reinvestment), but kept DCF at a meaningful 0.40 given the AI-disruption uncertainty. Reconciled IV ~$136 implies ~46% upside vs $93.01 — consistent with a quality compounder whose multiple over-corrected on fear rather than fundamentals. Key risk to the thesis: if AI genuinely disrupts the workflow-platform moat, the 32x fair multiple and growth assumptions are too generous.
